questions.question_text: Have you identified the main business drivers?
questions.guidance: Example business drivers: cyber crime prevention, risk reduction, law / regulation, audit / compliance, business continuity

questions.question_text: Have you documented the main business drivers?
questions.guidance: Documentation of business drivers is important for demonstrable business alignment

questions.question_text: Do you use business drivers in the decision making process?
questions.guidance: e.g. to determine priorities or make decisions regarding the on-boarding of new services or operations

questions.question_text: Do you regularly check if the current service catalogue is aligned with business drivers?
questions.guidance: i.e. do you check for services or operations that outside the scope of business drivers?

questions.question_text: Have the business drivers been validated with business stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Business stakeholders can be C-level management

questions.question_text: Have you identified the SOC customers & stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Types of customers and stakeholders, their requirements, expectations, etc.

questions.question_text: Have you documented the main SOC customers & stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Formal registration of customer & stakeholder contact details, function, agreements, etc.

questions.question_text: Do you differentiate output towards these specific customers & stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Differentiating output is helpful to match expectations of customers & stakeholders

questions.question_text: Do you have service level agreements with these customers & stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Service level agreements are used to provide standardized services operating within known boundaries

questions.question_text: Do you regularly send updates to your customers & stakeholders?
questions.guidance: For example: changes in service scope or delivery. Can also be reports, dashboards, etc.

questions.question_text: Do you actively measure and manage customer & stakeholder satisfaction?
questions.guidance: Understanding customer & stakeholder satisfaction will help to better align with business needs

questions.question_text: Does the SOC have a formal charter document in place?
questions.guidance: See 3.2 for charter document elements

questions.question_text: Is the SOC charter document regularly updated?
questions.guidance: Regularity should be matched to your own internal policy. At least yearly is recommended

questions.question_text: Is the SOC charter document approved by the business / CISO?
questions.guidance: Approval from the relevant stakeholders will aid in business support for SOC operations

questions.question_text: Are all stakeholders familiar with the SOC charter document contents?
questions.guidance: Making stakeholders aware of the contents helps in getting organizational support for security operations

questions.question_text: Does the SOC have a governance process in place?
questions.guidance: A governance process is required to determine the way the SOC should be managed

questions.question_text: Have all governance elements been identified?
questions.guidance: Possible governance elements can be found in under 4.3
Managing costs is required to justify budget allocation for the SOC and ensure continued service delivery in the future

questions.question_text: Is the governance process regularly reviewed?
questions.guidance: Frequency should be matched to your own internal policy. At least yearly is recommended

questions.question_text: Is the governance process aligned with all stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Alignment will help the SOC obtain required mandate, budget and management support

questions.question_text: Is the SOC regularly audited or subjected to (external) assessments?
questions.guidance: Frequency should be matched to the SOC policy. At least yearly is recommended. 3rd party assessments have a higher objectivity

questions.question_text: Is there an active cooperation with other SOCs (external)?
questions.guidance: External collaboration and networking, exchaning best practices, threat intelligence, and response actions with other SOCs

questions.question_text: Is a privacy policy regarding security monitoring of employees in place?
questions.guidance: A privacy policy should state that monitoring of employees is possible within acceptable limits

questions.question_text: Does the SOC operate in compliance with all applicable privacy laws and regulations?
questions.guidance: Local laws and regulations as well as company policy may apply and should all be considered

questions.question_text: Does the SOC cooperate with legal departments regarding privacy matters?
questions.guidance: Cooperation will ensure that the SOC is enabled to perform activities, rather than blocked

questions.question_text: Are specific procedures in place for dealing with privacy related investigations?
questions.guidance: Privacy related issues require careful examination, especially those potentially leading to court cases

questions.question_text: Is the SOC aware of all information that it processes and is subject to privacy regulations?
questions.guidance: Such information includes IP addresses, customer identifiers, user names, host names (for personally owned devices), etc.

questions.question_text: Is a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) regularly conducted?
questions.guidance: Can be used to determine the impact of monitoring on privacy, and can help uncover potential violations

questions.question_text: Does the current size of the SOC meet FTE requirements?
questions.guidance: i.e. is the SOC size sufficient to realize business goals?

questions.question_text: Does the SOC meet requirements for internal to external employee FTE ratio?
questions.guidance: Note: requirements do not need to be explicit. Set importance to 'None' if you have no external employees.

questions.question_text: Does the SOC meet requirements for internal to external employee skillset?
questions.guidance: i.e. Are there any crucial skills amongst external employees? Set importance to 'None' if you have no external employees
Unfilled positions may be due to deficiencies in the recruitment process

questions.question_text: Do you have a recruitment process in place?
questions.guidance: A recruitment process is required to obtain new employees in a market where talent is scarce

questions.question_text: Do you have a talent acquisition process in place?
questions.guidance: Talent sourcing can be vital for SOC success

questions.question_text: Do you formally differentiate roles within the SOC?
questions.guidance: Use the roles in 2.2 to determine if you have all roles required in the SOC

questions.question_text: Do you differentiate tiers within these roles?
questions.guidance: If you have no tiers, and you feel this is not a restriction, select importance 'None'
Consider the staffing levels (desired FTE count) as well as knowledge and experience for all roles

questions.question_text: Is there a role-based hierarchy in your SOC?
questions.guidance: If you have no hierarchy, and you feel this is not a restriction, select importance 'None'

questions.question_text: Have you formally documented all SOC roles?
questions.guidance: Possible documentation elements can be found in under 2.7

questions.question_text: Are responsibilities for each role understood?
questions.guidance: Responsibilities for each role should be clearly understood by all SOC personnel

questions.question_text: Have you documented career progression requirements for each of these roles?
questions.guidance: Career progression for roles can be documented through training, certification, experience and soft skills requirements

questions.question_text: Do you regularly revise or update the role descriptions?
questions.guidance: To revise is to review and verify whether to documentation is still correct or requires an update

questions.question_text: Do you have a job rotation plan in place?
questions.guidance: Job rotation can be used to train employees in a variety of tasks and avoid too much routine

questions.question_text: Do you have a career progression process in place?
questions.guidance: Career development, promotion, etc.

questions.question_text: Do you have a talent management process in place?
questions.guidance: Talent should be adequately managed to retain such staff and fully develop their potential.

questions.question_text: Do you have team diversity goals?
questions.guidance: e.g. background diversity, ethnic diversity, gender diversity, etc.

questions.question_text: Do you periodically evaluate SOC employees?
questions.guidance: Can also be included  in the regular organization evaluation process

questions.question_text: Do you have a 'new hire' process in place?
questions.guidance: i.e. a defined process to quickly let new employees find their place and perform well in the SOC

questions.question_text: Are all SOC employees subjected to screening?
questions.guidance: Personnel screening is performed to avoid infiltration or misbehaviour by SOC employees

questions.question_text: Do you measure employee satisfaction for improving the SOC?
questions.guidance: Employee satisfaction should be taken seriously as lack of satisfaction may lead to key personnel leaving

questions.question_text: Are there regular 1-on-1 meetings between the SOC manager and the employees?
questions.guidance: Such informal 1-on-1 conversations are used to coach employees and help the SOC manager gain insight in personal challenges

questions.question_text: Do you perform regular teambuilding exercises?
questions.guidance: Teambuilding exercises are used to promote collaboration between individuals in the team and to raise team spirit

questions.question_text: Do you have a formal knowledge management process in place?
questions.guidance: Formal knowledge management helps to optimize knowledge creation and distribution

questions.question_text: Do you regularly assess and revise the knowledge management process?
questions.guidance: This refers to the knowledge management process as a whole

questions.question_text: Is there effective tooling in place to support knowledge documentation and distribution?
questions.guidance: Such tooling can help to avoid investigation similar issues multiple times by integrating into the security monitoring process

questions.question_text: Do you have a training program in place?
questions.guidance: A training program is used to ensure a minimal level of knowledge for employees

questions.question_text: Do you have a certification program in place?
questions.guidance: A certification program is used to provide a demonstrable minimum level of knowledge and skills

questions.question_text: Is the training and certification program connected to evaluation and career progression?
questions.guidance: e.g. certain training and certifications are required to grow from a junior level function to a more senior level function

questions.question_text: Is there a reserved budget for education and training?
questions.guidance: i.e. a fixed percentage of the total SOC budget that is allocated for education and cannot be used for other purposes

questions.question_text: Is there a reserved amount of time for education and training?
questions.guidance: This is an extension of education budget

questions.question_text: Do you have regular workshops for knowledge development?
questions.guidance: Workshops are an informal way of distributing knowledge

questions.question_text: Do you regularly revise and update the training and certification programs?
questions.guidance: Training and certification must be a relevant reflection of SOC knowledge and skill requirements

questions.question_text: Is there a SOC management process in place?
questions.guidance: A SOC management process is used to manage all aspects SOC service delivery and quality

questions.question_text: Are SOC management elements formally identified and documented?
questions.guidance: Possible SOC management elements can be found in under 1.3

questions.question_text: Is the SOC management process regularly reviewed?
questions.guidance: Regular review of the SOC management process ensures optimal performance

questions.question_text: Is the SOC management process aligned with all stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Alignment with stakeholders will ensure the SOC delivers services that meet customer expectations

questions.question_text: Do you perform security operations exercises regularly?
questions.guidance: Regularity should be matched to your own internal policy

questions.question_text: Do you have standard operating procedures?
questions.guidance: Standard operating procedures are used to provide consistent output

questions.question_text: Do you use checklists for recurring activities?
questions.guidance: Checklists can be useful to avoid recurring activities from being overlooked
Workflows are used to standardize steps in, for example, security analysis

questions.question_text: Do you have a SOC operational handbook?
questions.guidance: A SOC operational handbook contains an overview of SOC tasks, as well as rules of engagement and expected behaviour

questions.question_text: Do you have a Document Management System in place?
questions.guidance: The system should support different file types, authorizations and version management; possibly even encryption

questions.question_text: Do you have a knowledge & collaboration platform in place?
questions.guidance: e.g. a wiki space or SharePoint that allows collaboration and supports team efforts

questions.question_text: Is there a use case management process or framework in place?
questions.guidance: A framework, such as MaGMa UCF[1], can be used to guide use case lifecycle and document use case in a standardized format
Formal documentation may include use case documentation templates

questions.question_text: Are use cases approved by relevant stakeholders?
questions.guidance: e.g. business stakeholders, IT stakeholders, CISOs, audit & compliance, risk management, etc.

questions.question_text: Is the use case management process aligned with other important processes?
questions.guidance: e.g. integration with the threat / risk management process to revise use cases when the threat landscape changes

questions.question_text: Are use cases created using a standardized process?
questions.guidance: i.e. a standardized approach to derive use cases from threats or business requirements

questions.question_text: Are use cases created using a top-down approach?
questions.guidance: e.g. use cases can be derived from business requirements, risk assessments, threat management / intelligence

questions.question_text: Can use cases be traced from high-level drivers to low-level implementation?
questions.guidance: Top-down traceability is important to determine completeness of implementation and demonstrable risk reduction

questions.question_text: Can use cases be traced from low-level implementation to high-level drivers?
questions.guidance: Bottom-up traceability is important for contextualizing use case output and business alignment

questions.question_text: Are use cases measured for implementation and effectiveness?
questions.guidance: Metrics can be applied to use cases to determine growth and maturity by measuring effectiveness and implementation

questions.question_text: Are use cases scored and prioritized based on risk levels?
questions.guidance: Risks can be (cyber)threats, but also non-compliance or penalties (laws & regulations)

questions.question_text: Are use cases regularly revised and updated?
questions.guidance: Use cases should be subjected to life cycle management and may require updates or may be outdated and decommissioned

questions.guidance: Functional ownership includes functional accountability

questions.question_text: Has technical ownership of the solution been formally assigned?
questions.guidance: Technical ownership includes technical accountability

questions.question_text: Has the solution been technically documented?
questions.guidance: A technical description of the system's components and configuration

questions.question_text: Has the solution been functionally documented?
questions.guidance: A description of the system's functional configuration (workflows, integrations, etc.)

questions.question_text: Is the personnel for support formally trained?
questions.guidance: Training helps to jump start new hires, and to learn a proper way of working with the tool

questions.question_text: Is the personnel for support certified?
questions.guidance: Certification demonstrates ability to handle the tooling properly

questions.question_text: Is there a support contract for the solution?
questions.guidance: A support contract may cover on-site support, support availability, response times, escalation and full access to resources

questions.question_text: Is there high availability (HA) in place for the solution?
questions.guidance: Can be fully implemented HA, partially implemented, hot spare, etc.

questions.question_text: Is there data backup / replication in place for the solution?

questions.question_text: Is there configuration backup / replication in place for the solution?

questions.question_text: Have you formally described the security monitoring service?
questions.guidance: A service description should be in place

questions.question_text: Is the service measured for quality?
questions.guidance: Are the quality indicators from the previous questions used for reporting on the service?

questions.question_text: Is the service measured for service delivery in accordance with service levels?
questions.guidance: Service levels should be used to formally commit the SOC to service delivery

questions.question_text: Are customers and/or stakeholders regularly updated about the service?
questions.guidance: Changes to the service scope, delivery, etc.

questions.question_text: Is there a contractual agreement between the SOC and the customers?
questions.guidance: Contractual agreements should also cover penalties

questions.question_text: Is sufficient personnel allocated to the process to ensure required service delivery?
questions.guidance: Allocation of dedicated personnel will ensure highest service quality

questions.question_text: Is the service aligned with other relevant processes?
questions.guidance: e.g. alignment with configuration management, incident management, etc.

questions.question_text: Is there a incident resolution / service continuity process in place for this service?
questions.guidance: Service continuity is important to comply with contractual agreements, even in case of major incidents

questions.question_text: Has a set of procedures been created for this service?
questions.guidance: Procedures support process standardization and quality. Personnel should be trained to use procedures correctly and structurally

questions.question_text: Are best practices applied to the service?

questions.question_text: Are use cases used in the security monitoring service?

questions.question_text: Is process data gathered for prediction of service performance?

questions.question_text: Is the service continuously being improved based on improvement goals?

Formal closure of the incident, including debriefing sessions

questions.question_text: Are ITSM processes integrated in the SOC?
questions.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's ITSM processes

questions.question_text: Are ITSM processes integrations regularly evaluated?
questions.guidance: ITSM process integrations must be regularly evaluated to find optimizations and shortcomings

questions.question_text: Have you implemented shifts in the SOC?
questions.guidance: Shifts are required for reliable and consistent service delivery in the SOC

questions.question_text: Do you have an automation engineering process in place?
questions.guidance: An automation engineering process supports the creation and deployment of automations in the SOC

questions.question_text: Is the automation engineering process formally documented?
questions.guidance: Formal documentation supports process standardisation, and allows for faster training of new engineers

questions.question_text: Are there specific roles and requirements for automation engineers?
questions.guidance: Automation engineers have a skillset that is different from security analysts and security engineers

questions.question_text: Are automations tracked and measured using defined metrics?
questions.guidance: Tracking automation effectiveness is important to measure and optimize the impact of automations on SOC effectiveness

questions.question_text: Are all SOC use cases touched or resolved by automation?
questions.guidance: In an automation-first strategy, all SOC uses should be touch and resolved much as possible

questions.question_text: Are custom automation playbooks developed in the SOC?
questions.guidance: Custom automation playbooks are tailored to specific needs of the SOC and its customers

questions.question_text: Is there a testing procedure to test and validate automations?
questions.guidance: Validating automations should be done before deployment, and after major changes

questions.question_text: Is there a formal release process in place for new automations?
questions.guidance: A release process ensures that automations are deployed in production in a predicatble and reliable way

questions.question_text: Do you have a AI adoption strategy for the SOC in place?
questions.guidance: An AI adoption strategy will help define the direction of AI within the SOC

questions.question_text: Is the AI adoption strategy internally aligned and approved by relevant stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Internal alignment with relevant stakeholders will ensure the SOC is operating in alignment with the broader AI strategy

questions.question_text: Is there a log management process in place?
questions.guidance: An log management process is used to manage logs throughout their lifecycle

questions.question_text: Are log management elements formally identified and documented?
questions.guidance: Formal documentation supports process standardisation, and allows for faster training of new engineers

questions.question_text: Is the log management process supported by corporate policy?
questions.guidance: The main relevant policies are auditing & logging policy, data handling and privacy policies

questions.question_text: Is the log management process supported by appropriate centralised log management tooling?
questions.guidance: Centralised log management tooling provides technical capabilities that support the process. May be part of the SIEM solution

questions.question_text: Is the log management process compliant with applicable standards & regulations?
questions.guidance: Logs must be handled in compliance with internal and external regulations, including privacy

questions.question_text: Is the log management process aligned with all stakeholders?
questions.guidance: Relevant stakeholders include privacy office, data protection office, and other risk & security stakeholders

questions.question_text: Is logging encrypted in transfer, in use, and at rest?
questions.guidance: Data encryption throughout the full lifecycle is a necessity for confidentiality

questions.question_text: Is access to logging restricted to authorized personnel?
questions.guidance: Access must be restricted using leas privilege and need to know principles
